Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Oscar Wilde (author, Wikidata Q30875), died 1900; Aubrey Beardsley (illustrator, Wikidata Q272566), died 1898; Hedwig Lachmann (translator, Wikidata Q72070), died 1918. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Wilde, Oscar, 1854-1900; Beardsley, Aubrey, 1872-1898 [Illustrator]; Lachmann, Hedwig, 1865-1918 [Translator]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: Salome, Tragoedie in einem Akt, Leipzig, Im Insel-Verlage, 1900, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/salometragoediei00wild. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 95%, 88%, 100% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Aubrey Beardsley, Hedwig Lachmann, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
